opening_message:
Ticket 1: Robert Weber (employee ID E047) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E047.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Robert Weber (E047) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Source Code. Full-time employees max out at write unless their role owns the system; Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Payroll Specialist, so maximum is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Robert Weber (E047) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors never get admin; with basic training the maximum is read. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: HR's record (authoritative for employment status) lists E047 as full-time Payroll Specialist. Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Payroll Specialist, so full-time employees cannot have admin here; the maximum is write. The requested admin exceeds the maximum, so I grant the maximum of write. (Note: the Security note claims contractor status, creating a conflict; I defer to HR's employment record, which yields the higher maximum of write, but still no admin.)

- Note 2 (Security?): employment type contractor, security training basic. Recommendation: read. Contractors never admin; basic training max read.

The two notes conflict on employment type: full_time vs contractor. Also conflict on recommendation: write vs read.

Note 1 says employment type full_time (looked up in own database). Note 2 also says employment type contractor (looked up in own database). Conflict on employment type.

The recommendation differs: write vs read. For full-time employee, max write. For contractor with basic training, max read.

The requested level is admin. In both cases, admin exceeds the maximum, so the grant would be the maximum: write (if full-time) or read (if contractor).

We need to pick. Perhaps there's a tiebreaker: HR database is typically authoritative for employment type. The Security agent contradicts HR on employment type, which is HR's domain. But we don't know which agent wrote which note.
